claims.text: The starting material is FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy powder with a particle size of 15–45 μm.
Standard HVAF-i7 deposition of the 15–45 μm powder produces coatings of acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
The HVAF-i7 nozzle, gas flux, and spray distance should be modified, with spray distances targeted at 300–350 mm.
The proposed nozzle, gas-flux, and 300–350 mm spray-distance settings will increase particle velocity.
Increasing particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy.
Greater particle kinetic energy enhances splat flattening.
Greater particle kinetic energy improves interparticle bonding.
Higher particle kinetic energy will reduce coating porosity and produce a denser coating.
Improved impingement and splat formation increase the effective accumulation of material on the substrate.
The optimized process will increase deposition efficiency.
The optimized process will produce a significantly thicker coating than the unmodified HVAF-i7 baseline.
The thicker coating will retain sufficient adhesion.
The optimized coating will have low or minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Controlling thermal input and oxygen exposure is necessary to limit in-flight particle oxidation.
The intervention can remain effective in internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The deposition settings can ensure complete in-flight particle melting while controlling oxidation.
The controlled experiment compares modified and standard HVAF-i7 settings while holding feedstock, substrate, and environmental conditions constant.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thickness increase, or occurrence of unacceptable oxidation or adhesion loss, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats a 300–350 mm spray distance as part of a velocity- and thickness-enhancing intervention, but the cited spray-distance record states that increasing distance lowers impact kinetic energy and coating thickness while increasing porosity and oxide content. The record supplies no nozzle-specific evidence that 300–350 mm is optimal for HVAF-i7.
